title: 21. Projects: Social Media API
objectives: Build the Social Media API projects end to end
Keep a short README with assumptions and tradeoffs

sections.title: What You'll Build
sections.body:
A scalable social media backend handling:

- User profiles with follow/unfollow
- Posts with images/videos (CDN upload)
- News feed generation (fan-out pattern)
- Likes, comments, shares
- Real-time notifications (WebSocket)
- Hashtag trending system
- Content moderation

Key Design Decisions:
- Feed is PRE-COMPUTED (not generated on request)
- Notifications use WebSocket (real-time)
- Images served from CDN (not your server)
- Write path: Post → Fan-out to followers' feeds

sections.title: Key Implementations
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Get user's feed (pre-computed in Redis)
- Push post to all followers' feeds (fan-out on write)
- Track trending hashtags using Redis sorted sets
- Increment hashtag count in current time window
- Indexes for both directions
- Check if already following
- Update counters (denormalized for fast profile loads)
- Notify target user (async)

**Defines:** `Follow`, `SocialService`, `FeedService`, `NotificationManager`, `notification_ws()`, `TrendingService`

### Follow System (PostgreSQL — Relational Data)

```python
# app/models/social.py
class Follow(Base):
    __tablename__ = "follows"

    follower_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"), primary_key=True)
    following_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"), primary_key=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now())

    # Indexes for both directions
    __table_args__ = (
        Index("idx_follower", "follower_id"),
        Index("idx_following", "following_id"),
    )

# app/services/social_service.py
class SocialService:
    async def follow_user(self, follower_id: int, target_id: int):
        if follower_id == target_id:
            raise ValueError("Cannot follow yourself")

        # Check if already following
        existing = await self.db.execute(
            select(Follow).where(
                Follow.follower_id == follower_id,
                Follow.following_id == target_id
            )
        )
        if existing.scalar_one_or_none():
            raise ValueError("Already following")

        follow = Follow(follower_id=follower_id, following_id=target_id)
        self.db.add(follow)

        # Update counters (denormalized for fast profile loads)
        await self.db.execute(
            update(User).where(User.id == follower_id)
            .values(following_count=User.following_count + 1)
        )
        await self.db.execute(
            update(User).where(User.id == target_id)
            .values(followers_count=User.followers_count + 1)
        )

        await self.db.commit()

        # Notify target user (async)
        from app.tasks.notification_tasks import send_follow_notification
        send_follow_notification.delay(target_id, follower_id)

    async def get_feed(self, user_id: int, page: int = 1, limit: int = 20):
        """Get user's feed (pre-computed in Redis)"""
        cache_key = f"feed:{user_id}"
        start = (page - 1) * limit
        end = start + limit - 1

        # Try pre-computed feed from Redis
        post_ids = await self.redis.lrange(cache_key, start, end)

        if not post_ids:
            # Fallback: Generate feed from DB (slower)
            return await self._generate_feed_from_db(user_id, page, limit)

        # Fetch full posts from MongoDB
        posts = []
        for post_id in post_ids:
            post = await self.mongo.posts.find_one({"_id": ObjectId(post_id)})
            if post:
                posts.append(post)

        return posts
```

### News Feed — Fan-Out Pattern

```python
# How Instagram/Twitter generates your feed:

# When a user creates a post:
class FeedService:
    async def fan_out_post(self, author_id: int, post_id: str):
        """Push post to all followers' feeds (fan-out on write)"""

        # Get all followers
        result = await self.db.execute(
            select(Follow.follower_id).where(Follow.following_id == author_id)
        )
        follower_ids = [row[0] for row in result.all()]

        # For each follower, prepend to their feed in Redis
        pipe = self.redis.pipeline()
        for follower_id in follower_ids:
            feed_key = f"feed:{follower_id}"
            pipe.lpush(feed_key, post_id)      # Add to front of feed
            pipe.ltrim(feed_key, 0, 499)        # Keep only latest 500 posts
            pipe.expire(feed_key, 86400 * 7)    # Expire after 7 days

        await pipe.execute()

# Two approaches to feeds:
#
# Fan-Out on Write (Instagram approach):
#   When user posts → Push to ALL followers' feeds immediately
#   ✅ Reading feed is INSTANT (pre-computed)
#   ❌ Expensive for users with millions of followers (celebrities)
#
# Fan-Out on Read (Twitter approach for high-follower accounts):
#   When user opens app → Generate feed by pulling from followed users
#   ✅ Cheap to write
#   ❌ Slow to read (must compute on every request)
#
# Hybrid (What Twitter/Instagram actually use):
#   Regular users → Fan-out on write
#   Celebrities (>500K followers) → Fan-out on read (merge at read time)
```

### Real-Time Notifications (WebSocket)

```python
# app/api/notifications.py
from fastapi import WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect

class NotificationManager:
    def __init__(self):
        self.connections: dict[int, WebSocket] = {}

    async def connect(self, user_id: int, websocket: WebSocket):
        await websocket.accept()
        self.connections[user_id] = websocket

    async def disconnect(self, user_id: int):
        self.connections.pop(user_id, None)

    async def send_notification(self, user_id: int, notification: dict):
        ws = self.connections.get(user_id)
        if ws:
            await ws.send_json(notification)
        # Also save to DB for when user is offline
        await self.save_notification(user_id, notification)

notification_manager = NotificationManager()

@app.websocket("/ws/notifications")
async def notification_ws(websocket: WebSocket):
    token = websocket.query_params.get("token")
    user = verify_token(token)

    await notification_manager.connect(user.id, websocket)
    try:
        while True:
            # Keep connection alive, handle client messages
            data = await websocket.receive_json()
            if data.get("type") == "mark_read":
                await mark_notification_read(data["notification_id"])
    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        await notification_manager.disconnect(user.id)
```

### Hashtag Trending System

```python
# app/services/trending_service.py
import time

class TrendingService:
    """Track trending hashtags using Redis sorted sets"""

    def __init__(self, redis_client):
        self.redis = redis_client

    async def track_hashtag(self, hashtag: str):
        """Increment hashtag count in current time window"""
        hour_key = f"trending:{int(time.time() // 3600)}"  # Current hour bucket
        await self.redis.zincrby(hour_key, 1, hashtag.lower())
        await self.redis.expire(hour_key, 86400)  # Keep for 24 hours

    async def get_trending(self, count: int = 10) -> list:
        """Get top trending hashtags from last 6 hours"""
        current_hour = int(time.time() // 3600)
        keys = [f"trending:{current_hour - i}" for i in range(6)]

        # Union last 6 hours with weights (recent = higher weight)
        dest_key = "trending:combined"
        weights = [6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # Recent hours weighted more

        await self.redis.zunionstore(dest_key, dict(zip(keys, weights)))
        await self.redis.expire(dest_key, 300)  # Cache for 5 min

        # Get top hashtags
        results = await self.redis.zrevrange(dest_key, 0, count - 1, withscores=True)
        return [{"hashtag": h, "score": int(s)} for h, s in results]
```

sections.title: API Endpoints
sections.body:
```
User Profiles:
  GET    /users/{username}          ← Public profile
  PUT    /users/me                  ← Update own profile
  POST   /users/{id}/follow         ← Follow user
  DELETE /users/{id}/follow         ← Unfollow user
  GET    /users/{id}/followers      ← List followers
  GET    /users/{id}/following      ← List following

Posts:
  POST   /posts                     ← Create post (with media)
  GET    /posts/{id}                ← Get single post
  DELETE /posts/{id}                ← Delete own post
  POST   /posts/{id}/like           ← Like post
  DELETE /posts/{id}/like           ← Unlike post
  GET    /posts/{id}/comments       ← Get comments

Feed:
  GET    /feed                      ← User's personalized feed
  GET    /explore                   ← Discover/trending posts

Notifications:
  GET    /notifications             ← List notifications
  WS     /ws/notifications          ← Real-time notifications

Trending:
  GET    /trending/hashtags         ← Trending hashtags
  GET    /hashtag/{tag}             ← Posts with hashtag
```

sections.title: What You Learned
sections.body:
- Fan-out pattern for news feed generation
- Denormalization for fast reads
- WebSocket-based real-time notifications
- Redis sorted sets for trending/ranking
- CDN integration for media
- Hybrid fan-out strategy (write + read)
